key_patterns.name: Multiplex homophily
key_patterns.description: Edges cluster by age_group and occupation with dense family and work/school layers and sparser community ties. Overlap across layers creates strong ties.
key_patterns.relevance: Homophily and layer strength amplify local conformity; calibrate layer weights and assortativity to reproduce clustered adoption cascades.

key_patterns.name: Risk-driven predisposition
key_patterns.description: Higher risk_perception should correlate with higher initial adoption and stronger response to pro-mask signals.
key_patterns.relevance: Map risk_perception to agent thresholds/susceptibility; informs heterogeneity needed to match early uptake and retention.

key_patterns.name: Adoption persistence (habit)
key_patterns.description: wearing_mask tends to persist day-to-day; drop events are rarer than adoptions during growth phases.
key_patterns.relevance: Include retention (habit) parameter to capture inertia; crucial for retention_rate and switching_rate calibration.

key_patterns.name: Information-to-behavior linkage
key_patterns.description: received_info is expected to increase next-day adoption probability, especially when neighbors are adopters.
key_patterns.relevance: Estimate effect sizes for information vs. social exposure to calibrate behavior_reproduction_number and peak_adoption_velocity.

key_patterns.name: Layered exposure asymmetry
key_patterns.description: Family contacts likely exert stronger influence per tie than work/school, which in turn exceeds community ties.
key_patterns.relevance: Set layer-specific influence weights and info-transmission probabilities to reproduce realistic diffusion speeds.

key_patterns.name: Network directionality and duplicates
key_patterns.description: JSON adjacency may be asymmetric and contain duplicate neighbors across layers.
key_patterns.relevance: Symmetrization and deduplication affect degree distributions and exposure computation; must be standardized pre-calibration.

key_distributions.name: Risk perception
key_distributions.description: Continuous in [0,1]; often well-modeled by a Beta distribution reflecting skew toward moderate or high perceived risk.
key_distributions.parameters: Fit Beta(alpha, beta) via MLE or method-of-moments on agent_attributes.risk_perception.

key_distributions.name: Degree by layer
key_distributions.description: Family degrees are small with low variance; work/school degrees moderate; community degrees heavy-tailed.
key_distributions.parameters: Fit per-layer degree distributions: Family ~ Poisson(lambda_fam), Work/School ~ Poisson/NegBin(k_ws, p_ws), Community ~ Negative Binomial (r_comm, p_comm).

key_distributions.name: Initial adoption
key_distributions.description: Distribution of wearing_mask at day 0 across agents; varies with risk_perception and demographics.
key_distributions.parameters: Estimate p0 overall and by strata: p0 = mean(wearing_mask at day 0); optionally p0_i via logistic(a0 + a1*risk_i + strata fixed effects).

key_distributions.name: Daily adoption/drop hazards
key_distributions.description: Transition probabilities for adopt (0→1) and drop (1→0) conditional on exposures and info.
key_distributions.parameters: Hazard models: P(adopt_t+1 | state_t, exposures_t, info_t) = logistic(β0 + β•features); same for drop with coefficients δ.

key_distributions.name: Exposure shares
key_distributions.description: Per-day share of masked neighbors by layer for each agent.
key_distributions.parameters: Compute exposure_lit = masked_neighbors_lit / degree_l for l in {family, work_school, community}; aggregate as weighted sum with weights w_l.

key_relationships.relationship: Positive effect of receiving pro-mask info on next-day adoption controlling for prior state.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate via logistic regression; expected medium-to-strong.

key_relationships.relationship: Higher masked-share among neighbors increases adoption probability; family effect > work/school > community.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate separate coefficients per layer; expected gradient family > work/school > community.

key_relationships.relationship: Higher risk perception raises baseline adoption and reduces propensity to drop.
key_relationships.strength: Expected strong for baseline; medium for incremental effects.

key_relationships.relationship: Group fixed effects reflect different baselines and responsiveness (e.g., students to school policies, workers to workplace mandates).
key_relationships.strength: Estimate via categorical fixed effects; expected medium.

key_relationships.relationship: Mandates/broadcasts shift intercept and may amplify social influence (multiplicative).
key_relationships.strength: To be estimated; effect size used for policy_impact metric.

layer_weights.notes: Calibrate by maximizing fit to adoption_rate_over_time and assortativity_by_adoption; weights scale exposure aggregation across layers.

symmetrize_edges.notes: Use undirected edges for influence unless explicitly modeling direction.

deduplicate_multi_layer_edges.value: Collapse duplicates across layers but track multiplicity
deduplicate_multi_layer_edges.notes: If a tie exists in multiple layers, either (a) keep one edge and increase effective weight, or (b) keep separate edges with layer-specific weights.

degree_distributions.value: Fit Family~Poisson, Work/School~Poisson or NegBin, Community~NegBin
degree_distributions.notes: Use fitted parameters to generate synthetic networks or validate provided graph.

assortativity_targets.value: Compute by adoption state each day; target baseline level at early-mid simulation
assortativity_targets.notes: Use as calibration target to match clustering of adopters.

threshold_mapping.notes: Lower threshold => easier adoption; refine via regression linking risk to adoption given exposures.

initial_state_model.notes: Seed initial states from observed day 0 if available; otherwise sample from this model using estimated coefficients.

susceptibility_scaler.value: lambda_i = 1 + k*risk_i with k=1.0 (to be calibrated)
susceptibility_scaler.notes: Scales social influence weight for each agent.

social_influence_coefficients.source: daily panel CSV exposures vs. transitions + social_network.json
social_influence_coefficients.notes: Initial priors; calibrate via logistic regression of adoption on layer-specific exposure shares.

habit_persistence.notes: Baseline retention probability absent info/policy; critical for retention_rate.

spontaneous_adoption.source: daily panel CSV P(adopt | zero exposure and no info)
spontaneous_adoption.notes: Captures exogenous influences; refine via periods with minimal exposure.

spontaneous_drop.source: daily panel CSV P(drop | no info and low neighbor adoption)
spontaneous_drop.notes: Controls steady-state; adjust to match final_adoption_rate.

decision_rule.value: Adopt if w·exposure_t + pi*policy_t + phi*info_t + u_i + ε_t >= theta_i
decision_rule.notes: w is vector of layer weights*coefficients; u_i can include demographic fixed/random effects; ε_t ~ Logistic(0, s) with s to calibrate.

neighbor_info_prob.source: daily panel CSV P(received_info_t | neighbor states by layer)
neighbor_info_prob.notes: Per-day probability a masked neighbor generates info for ego; calibrate jointly with social influence.

exogenous_broadcast_rate.source: daily panel CSV base rate of received_info when neighbors are unmasked
exogenous_broadcast_rate.notes: Can be time-varying to represent media shocks.

info_decay.value: carryover factor ρ=0.5 for info effects to persist 1 additional day
info_decay.notes: Models short memory of information exposure.

mandate_effect_on_threshold.source: Observed shifts in adoption around policy start dates (if present)
mandate_effect_on_threshold.notes: Subtract from theta_i or add to decision utility; occupation-specific multipliers can be estimated.

mandate_layer_enforcement.notes: Scales layer influence under mandate scenarios.

retention_window_days.notes: Window to compute retention_rate of adopters.

early_diffusion_window_days.notes: Window for behavior_reproduction_number estimation before saturation.

attribution_rule_for_influence.notes: Used to compute influence_inequality (Gini of credits).

preprocessing_steps.purpose: Convert social_network.json keys to integers; ensure agent_id alignment with agent_attributes.csv and daily panel CSV.
Create undirected per-layer graphs; remove duplicates; optionally preserve multiplicity as edge weights.

preprocessing_steps.step: Compute per-layer degrees and exposure shares daily
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Features for transition models: masked neighbor share by layer and aggregated exposure.
Ensure valid inputs; use median by age_group/occupation for missing values.
Estimate initial adoption and transition hazards; derive retention and switching rates.

preprocessing_steps.step: Parse booleans and ensure panel completeness
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Cast wearing_mask/received_info to bool; check (day, agent_id) coverage and fill missing with last observation carried forward if appropriate.

calibration_strategy.calibration_approach: Two-stage estimation with simulation-based refinement: (1) Statistical estimation: Fit logistic (or complementary log-log) models for adoption and drop hazards using features: prior state, per-layer neighbor_mask_share, received_info, risk_perception, age_group and occupation fixed effects, and policy indicators. Fit separate model for received_info as a function of neighbor states to estimate info diffusion parameters. (2) Map coefficients to simulation parameters (layer weights, susceptibility, habit persistence). (3) Run the simulator and perform likelihood-free/SMM/ABC calibration to match macro metrics (adoption_rate_over_time, time_to_50_percent_adoption, peak_adoption_velocity, final_adoption_rate), plus network-sensitive targets (assortativity_by_adoption, influence_inequality). Iterate until convergence measured by minimized loss over these targets.
calibration_strategy.validation_strategy: Out-of-time and out-of-network validation. Hold out a contiguous time block (e.g., last 20% of days) and a random 10-20% of nodes or subgraphs. Validate on: (a) RMSE/MAE of adoption_rate_over_time and AUC of adoption curve, (b) Error in time_to_50_percent_adoption and final_adoption_rate, (c) Peak_adoption_velocity timing and magnitude, (d) Retention_rate and switching_rate by strata, (e) Early-phase behavior_reproduction_number (branching estimator: ratio of new adoptions attributable within early window to current adopters), (f) Assortativity_by_adoption trajectory and influence_inequality (Gini). Use posterior predictive checks and parametric bootstrap to quantify uncertainty.
key_variables_to_calibrate: threshold_mapping parameters (a0, a1 or direct theta_i rule)
policy effect sizes (intercept shift, layer enforcement multipliers)
group-level effects by age_group and occupation

file_summaries:
Semantic metadata summary for agent_attributes.csv

- Data structure and type
  - File type: CSV (flat, row-oriented).
  - Each row represents one agent; no nested structures.
  - Expected primary key: agent_id (unique integer).

- Meaning of columns
  - agent_id: Unique identifier for each agent; use as the foreign key when linking to network edges or time-series logs.
  - age_group: Categorical demographic bin (e.g., Youth, Young Adult, Middle Age). Static trait; informs homophily, contact rates, and policy sensitivity.
  - occupation: Categorical role (e.g., Student, Blue Collar, White Collar). Static trait; informs network layer membership (school, workplace), daily mixing patterns, and exposure contexts.
  - risk_perception: Continuous scalar in [0,1]; higher implies greater perceived risk of not masking. Serves as an individual-level propensity affecting baseline mask adoption and responsiveness to social/policy signals.

- Relationships or nested elements
  - No explicit nesting; one-to-one mapping of row to agent.
  - agent_id should map to nodes in the social network (e.g., an edges list) and to any behavior logs.
  - age_group and occupation can be used to construct multiplex networks (e.g., family, school/work, community layers) via homophily and layer-specific connection rules.

- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions
  - Agent initialization:
    - Assign each agent: id, age_group, occupation, initial risk_perception.
    - Initialize mask_wearing_state using a function of risk_perception (and optionally group-level priors).
  - Social influence dynamics:
    - Use risk_perception as an individual threshold/weight in updating mask_wearing_state based on neighbors’ behaviors (e.g., higher risk_perception lowers the social threshold for adoption, increases conformity weight).
    - Age_group and occupation adjust influence weights (peer effects stronger within same group/role) and exposure to different network layers.
  - Network formation and contact patterns:
    - Construct edges with homophily on age_group and occupation; create dense subgraphs for schools and workplaces, sparser community links across groups.
    - Use occupation to set daily contact rates and layer participation (Students: school layer; Blue/White Collar: workplace layer; cross-layer community contacts).
  - Policy/context effects:
    - Modulate compliance sensitivity by occupation/age_group (e.g., workplace mandates affect workers more).
    - Allow risk_perception to evolve over time due to information shocks or neighborhood masking prevalence.
  - Data hygiene expectations:
    - agent_id must be unique and contiguous or cross-referenced consistently.
    - age_group/occupation should come from a controlled vocabulary.
    - risk_perception should be bounded [0,1]; handle missing values with imputation or defaults before simulation.

Semantic metadata summary for social_network.json

- Overall data structure and type
  - JSON object (dictionary) where each top-level key is an agent ID (stringified integer).
  - Each value is an object with three fields containing arrays of integers (adjacency lists).

- Meaning of keys or columns
  - Top-level keys ("0", "1", …): unique agent IDs.
  - Nested keys:
    - family: IDs of household/family ties.
    - work_school: IDs of coworkers/classmates.
    - community: IDs of broader community contacts.
  - Array values: neighbor agent IDs; unweighted, layer-typed links.

- Relationships or nested elements
  - Multiplex (multi-layer) network: each agent has up to three separate neighbor lists, one per social layer.
  - Links are represented ego-centrically; reciprocity is not guaranteed in the file (may require symmetrization).
  - Overlap across layers may occur (the same neighbor can appear in multiple lists), implying potential multi-edge/stronger influence if aggregated.
  - IDs in lists should correspond to other top-level keys; keys are strings while neighbor IDs are integers (type normalization needed).

- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions
  - Agents: one per top-level key; maintain mask state and possibly layer-specific behaviors.
  - Networks: build three layer-specific graphs (family, work_school, community); optionally a combined graph with layer weights.
  - Interaction/influence: compute exposure per layer as the share of mask-wearing neighbors; aggregate with layer weights (e.g., family > work_school > community) to drive adoption/abandonment decisions.
  - Processing needs: convert IDs to a consistent type, deduplicate neighbors within layers, optionally enforce undirected edges, and precompute degree/neighbor sets per layer for efficient updates.

- Data structure and type:
  - Flat CSV table; one row per agent per day (panel/longitudinal format).
  - Composite primary key: (day, agent_id). Booleans may be serialized as strings; ensure proper parsing.

- Meaning of columns:
  - day: Discrete simulation timestep (integer).
  - agent_id: Unique identifier for each agent (integer).
  - wearing_mask: Agent’s behavioral state at that day (boolean).
  - received_info: Whether the agent received pro-mask information that day (boolean), via neighbors or external sources.

- Relationships and nesting:
  - No nested elements; all fields are atomic.
  - Temporal relationship across rows for the same agent_id captures state transitions over time.
  - Implicit dependency: wearing_mask at day t may depend on received_info and social influence at or before day t; the social network itself is not included.

- How this informs simulation entities/interactions:
  - Agent initialization: For day 0 (or earliest day), set each agent’s wearing_mask and received_info states from the data.
  - State transition rules: Use sequences across days (if present in the full file) to calibrate probabilities linking received_info and subsequent mask adoption/retention (e.g., P(wearing_mask_t+1 | received_info_t, wearing_mask_t)).
  - Information dynamics: received_info should be generated each day via network diffusion (neighbors’ states/messages) and/or exogenous broadcasts; calibrate baseline info exposure from observed rates.
  - Validation/training: Compare simulated daily adoption trajectories to the CSV trajectories to fit parameters (social influence strength, decay/persistence of wearing_mask, spontaneous adoption/abandonment rates).
  - Data gaps: Since the social graph isn’t provided here, supply or infer it externally; treat (day, agent_id) coverage as the schedule for stepping agents and computing metrics (e.g., daily proportion wearing masks).
